upd.title: updates
upd.note: Only one device is updated at a time. Recommended order: access points first, one at a time (after each one check that it is back in CAPsMAN), the router last — its reboot takes down the whole network including Wi-Fi and this page. Before a RouterOS install a backup pre-<version>-<date>.backup + .rsc is saved on the device.
upd.cred_note_active: The password is kept only in server memory, bound to this mktk-map session. It is never stored or logged. A running job keeps it until it finishes and then discards it.
upd.cred_note: The credentials are verified by logging in to all devices. They are kept only in server memory for 30 minutes and then discarded. Actions can be started only after entering them.
upd.latest_never: the available version has not been checked yet
upd.confirm_check:
Check for updates on "{name}"?
(nothing is installed or rebooted)
upd.confirm_install:
Install RouterOS {version} on "{name}" ({host})?

Currently running {running}. A backup is saved first, then the new version is downloaded and the device REBOOTS.
upd.confirm_fw:
Upgrade firmware {cur} → {new} on "{name}" ({host})?

The device will REBOOT.
upd.confirm_outage: "{name}" is a {role}: during the reboot the whole network including Wi-Fi and this page will be down for several minutes. The job keeps running on the server.
conn.title: connections
conn.load_summary: router load — poll duration and CPU
conn.load_note: “monitor” = the regular device poll (system, clients, Wi-Fi, DHCP…) every 30 s, “conntrack” = the connection table. The duration includes network and TLS; growth with the same number of rows means a busier router.
conn.note: Data from the router's connection tracking table every 10 s while this page is open (otherwise 30 s). Connections shorter than the interval may be missed. FT = FastTrack: RouterOS may not count transferred data for it, so values may be lower. The destination name comes from the router's DNS cache; the name the client itself asked for takes precedence.
conn.dns.off: Client DNS queries are not arriving yet. The router can send them to mktk-map via syslog (the router gets /system logging action mktkdns → {host}:{port} and a rule topics=dns).
conn.dns.enable: enable DNS log on the router
conn.dns.on_no_data: DNS log is enabled on the router ({remote}, topic {topic}), but no query has arrived yet.
conn.dns.no_query_lines: Packets arrive, but no line contains a query — see the sample below.
conn.dns.rejected: Packets came from an unexpected address: {list} — it is not among the configured devices.
conn.dns.check_port: Check that port {port}/udp is published in docker-compose and nothing blocks it.
conn.dns.unparsed: Some DNS log lines could not be recognised ({n}). Sample:
conn.ft_title: FastTrack — transferred data may be incomplete
conn.d.none_doh: none yet (or the client uses DoH / its own DNS)
conn.d.new_conns_title: newly captured connections (excluding those already running at startup)
conn.o.note: Statistics are computed from increments between polls (FastTrack connections may be missing) and kept for 7 days.
dns.title: DNS queries
dns.clients_note: Click a client to limit the domain table to its queries.
dns.domains_note: Click a domain to see all clients. new = first seen within the last 24 h (within the retained data). Hourly details are kept for {hourly} days, the daily summary for {daily} days.
dns.timeline_7d: the timeline covers only the last 7 days
iot.cred_hint: Browsing works without credentials. To make changes, enter the MikroTik credentials (kept in memory for 30 min only):
iot.domains_note: The router adds the IP addresses of allowed domains to the address list when the device asks for them via DNS. After adding a domain, restart the device (or wait until its DNS cache expires).
iot.learn_note: “Learn” lets the device reach the whole internet for the chosen time, enables DNS logging and shows where it connects. Meanwhile, pair it in the vendor's app, then allow only what it needs. The router has a safety net: the temporary access expires on its own.
iot.leftover_logging: DNS logging from learning is still enabled on the router (the app was probably restarted during learning).
iot.drops_note: From the router log (prefix {prefix}; the log keeps the last few thousand lines). Destination names from the router's DNS cache.
iot.nothing_yet: nothing yet — pair the device in the vendor's app
iot.no_audit: no changes from the app yet
iot.prompt_domain: Allow domain (edit it if you want it narrower/wider):
iot.confirm_subdomains:
Allow subdomains *.{d} too?
(OK = yes, Cancel = only {d})
iot.confirm_ip: Allow the IoT network to connect to {ip}? (static IP — stops working when the vendor changes the IP; a domain is better)
iot.confirm_port: Allow {proto}/{port} from device {src} to whitelisted addresses?
iot.confirm_learn: Let {name} ({ip}) reach the whole internet for {min} min and enable DNS logging?
bak.title: configuration backups
bak.pick_version: pick a version on the left
bak.info: Configuration export (/export terse over SSH, without passwords) every {h} h, right after a change (based on /system history, within 5 min) and before updates. A version is stored only when something changed.
bak.ssh_needed: Backups need the monitor account to be allowed to use SSH (it stays read-only, only from this server).
bak.confirm_key: The SSH key of {host} has changed. Confirm only if you know why (router reset/upgrade).
wifi.radios_note: Channel and power are reported by the CAPsMAN controller, noise floor by the AP itself. Signal comes from client registrations. SNR below 20 dB means lower speeds, below 15 dB an unstable connection.
wifi.spectrum_note: 802.15.4 channel k is centred at 2405 + 5·(k−11) MHz. Red: channels inside the band of some 2.4 GHz radio; orange: within 5 MHz of its edge. Thread and Zigbee channels are set in ⚙ settings on the overview.
wifi.no_radios: no radios (neither CAPsMAN nor local wireless returned data)
wifi.no_24: no 2.4 GHz radio with a channel
wifi.zb_unset: Thread/Zigbee channels are not set — add them in ⚙ settings on the overview.
wifi.weak_note: Clients with a signal of {dbm} dBm or worse. If a closer AP exists, the device is probably sticking to a distant one (sticky client) — lowering the distant AP's power or setting a minimum signal in the CAPsMAN access list helps.
topo.title: topology
topo.note: Built from the neighbour tables of the devices (/ip neighbor — MNDP, LLDP, CDP), refreshed every 5 minutes. Indirect neighbours seen through switches are filtered out. Unmanaged devices that announce themselves (e.g. other switches) are shown with a dashed frame.
topo.no_devices: No devices are configured yet — add them in ⚙ settings on the overview.
topo.no_neighbors: The devices did not report any neighbours. Make sure neighbour discovery is enabled (/ip neighbor discovery-settings set discover-interface-list=LAN) and that the monitor account can read /ip neighbor. Until then only CAPsMAN links are shown.
topo.legend.l2: seen only over a VLAN (physical link unknown)
